(Springfield, Missouri) | college = * [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]] (2021–2022) * [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] (2022–2026) | highlights = }} '''Trevon Brazile''' (born January 7, 2003) is an American [[college basketball]] player for the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]] of the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC). He previously played for the [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri Tigers]]. ==Early life and high school career== Brazile was born in [[Springfield, Missouri]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/4698719/trevon-brazile|publisher=[[ESPN]]|title=Trevon Brazile}} He grew up playing basketball and usually was a [[point guard]].{{Cite web|url=https://missouri.rivals.com/news/brazile-s-rapid-rise-stokes-excitement-for-future|website=[[Rivals.com]]|title=Brazile's rapid rise stokes excitement for future|date=January 21, 2022|author=Forde, Mitchell}} He first attended [[Parkview High School (Springfield, Missouri)|Parkview High School]] in Springfield, where he played basketball and averaged 11.2 points and 5.1 rebounds per game as a [[Junior (education year)|junior]], before transferring to [[Kickapoo High School (Springfield, Missouri)|Kickapoo High School]] as a [[Senior (education)|senior]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.news-leader.com/story/sports/high-school/2020/07/28/trevon-brazile-parkview-star-leaving-play-kickapoo-high-school/5434907002/|newspaper=[[Springfield News-Leader]]|title=Former Parkview star Trevon Brazile becomes latest Division I prospect to join Kickapoo|date=July 28, 2020|author=Wheeler, Wyatt D.}} At Kickapoo, Brazile helped them win a state championship and was named all-state and first-team all-conference while averaging 13.2 points and 7.5 rebounds per game.{{Cite web|url=https://arkansasrazorbacks.com/roster/trevon-brazile/|publisher=[[Arkansas Razorbacks]]|title=Trevon Brazile}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.news-leader.com/story/sports/high-school/2022/11/17/arkansas-trevon-brazile-dunk-nba-draft-prospect-razorbacks-sec-kickapoo-springfield/69655872007/|newspaper=[[Springfield News-Leader]]|title=Watch: Springfield standout Trevon Brazile might have had the dunk of the year in an Arkansas win|date=November 16, 2022|author=Wheeler, Wyatt D.}} Ranked a three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], the fourth-best recruit in the state and the 178th-best nationally by [[247Sports]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2022/mar/31/brazile-ex-mizzou-forward-plans-to-transfer-to/|newspaper=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]|title=Brazile, ex-Mizzou forward, plans to transfer to Arkansas|date=March 31, 2022|author=Davenport, Richard}}{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-springfield-news-leader/135946360/|newspaper=[[Springfield News-Leader]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=March 17, 2021|page=A4|title=Brazile's unstoppable|author=Wheeler, Wyatt D.}} {{Open access}} ==College career== Brazile joined Missouri for the 2021–22 season but missed the first eight games with a medical condition, then played in two games as a backup and started the final 22 games. He led the team with 43 blocks, placing fourth all-time for [[Freshman|freshmen]] in school history, and averaged 6.6 points and 5.1 rebounds per game.{{Cite news|url=https://www.columbiatribune.com/story/sports/college/tiger-extra/2022/03/09/mizzou-basketball-missouri-trevon-brazile-sec-tournament-2022/6773600001/|newspaper=[[Columbia Daily Tribune]]|title=How freshman Trevon Brazile became an important building block for Mizzou basketball|date=March 9, 2022|author=Kwiecinski, Chris}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2023/jun/28/muss-says-brazile-is-in-a-great-spot/|newspaper=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]|url-access=registration|title=Muss says Brazile is 'in a great spot'|author=Holt, Bob|date=June 28, 2023}} After head coach [[Cuonzo Martin]] was dismissed by the Tigers, Brazile entered the [[NCAA transfer portal]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-springfield-news-leader/135947253/|newspaper=[[Springfield News-Leader]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=April 1, 2022|page=B1|author=Wheeler, Wyatt D.|title=Trevon Brazille transferring from Missouri to Arkansas}} {{Open access}} He ultimately transferred to [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/arkansas/hogs-mens-basketball/hogs-land-missouri-transfer-trevon-brazile-eric-musselman#gid=ci029d7dca30002674&pid=011222-trevon-brazile-missouri-nelson|website=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=Missouri Transfer Trevon Brazile Commits to Razorbacks|date=March 30, 2022}} As a [[sophomore]] at Arkansas in 2022–23, Brazile appeared in the first nine games before suffering a [[torn ACL]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3980258/2022/12/07/arkansas-trevon-brazile-injury/|website=[[The Athletic]]|title=Arkansas' Trevon Brazile out for season with ACL tear: What it means for Razorbacks' title chances|date=December 7, 2022|author=Vecenie, Sam; Moore, CJ}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/prospect-profiles/nba-draft-scouting-report-arkansas-trevon-brazile#gid=ci02b6b27d50002645&pid=usatsi_19610344|website=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=NBA Draft Scouting Report: Arkansas' Trevon Brazile|date=January 31, 2023}} He averaged 11.8 points and six rebounds per game and made 38% of his shots from the 3-point range.{{Cite news|url=https://razorbackswire.usatoday.com/2023/06/27/more-like-it-brazile-tabbed-as-likely-first-rounder-by-usa-today/|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|title=More like it: Brazile tabbed as likely first-rounder by USA TODAY|date=June 27, 2023|author=Wayne, E.}} He was considered a potential second-round selection in the [[2023 NBA draft]] despite his injury but opted to return for another season. Entering the 2023–24 season, Brazile was selected preseason first-team All-[[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC), one of the 50 watch listed players for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year]] and one of 20 watch listed players for the [[Karl Malone Award]].{{Cite news|url=https://razorbackswire.usatoday.com/2023/11/06/trevon-brazile-named-as-first-team-all-sec-one-of-best-50-players-in-the-nation/|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|title=Trevon Brazile named as first-team All-SEC, one of best 50 players in the nation|date=November 6, 2023|author=Wayne, E.}} On April 8, 2024, Brazile declared for the [[2024 NBA draft]].{{cite web|author=Jonathan Givony|title=Arkansas' Brazile to NBA draft despite Hogs' apparent regime change|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/39901396/arkansas-brazile-nba-draft-hogs-apparent-regime-change|website=ESPN.com|date=April 8, 2024|access-date=April 10, 2024}} On June 4, 2024, Brazile announced he would be withdrawing from the transfer portal and return to Arkansas. ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics
